ratings.reason: Uploading existing footage clearly triggers source-conditioned reconstruction, and video reauthoring is a consequential use. The quote does not describe the resulting controls or output, so rebuildability and novelty are only moderately supported.

This is an unusually clean instance: a preliminary user design is ingested and encoded as latent conditioning for generation. The input-to-encoding mechanism is explicit and transferable, although the quote omits the subsequent generation and interface details.

Existing journal entries are transformed into personalized music, plainly making the output a function of user-produced material. The cross-modal move is interesting and reusable, but the supplied evidence provides no ingestion details or outcome evidence.

Quologue's exclusive dependence on users' existing highlight collections strongly establishes source conditioning and suggests a broadly reusable personal-corpus pattern. The quote does not state what is generated or show the on-screen ingestion flow, limiting mechanism clarity.

The quote gives a complete source-to-output transformation: multimodal diary records and metadata become context-matched VR experiences. It is highly representative and distinctive, though its immersive output and spatial reconstruction make direct transfer more specialized.

A user uploads an existing primer melody, then conditions selected models with it alongside parameters and filters. The workflow is concrete and transferable, but seed-based music generation is a competent rather than surprising application of the pattern.

Using an existing lo-fi user flow to generate privacy-review outputs is a clear, consequential source-conditioned move with transfer potential to other artifact reviews. “Three-tiered outputs” is insufficiently specific to reconstruct the interface or processing stages.

The evidence explicitly names the interface, source action, GAN processing, and synthetic image response, making this one of the clearest instances to rebuild. Its basic image-to-image structure is broadly reusable but comparatively conventional, and no outcome evidence is supplied.

The collage-to-video transformation is vivid and potentially meaningful, but participants appear to create the collage specifically for the generative activity. That conflicts with the pattern boundary requiring material pre-existing with respect to the request, while the physical-textile workflow also limits direct transfer.

The system extracts events and emotions from a letter and conditions a personalized story on them, giving a legible encode-then-generate mechanism. It is unclear whether the letter already existed or was written to specify this request, and the evidence contains no reported effect.

TubeLens clearly converts a pre-existing personal history into an inferred visual-and-textual self-portrait for reflection. The source, transformation, and output are explicit; only the precise import/consent interaction and reconstruction details are absent.

Designer-specified clothing images directly condition generation of new sketches in the designer's style, making the source artifact central rather than incidental. The pattern is clear and portable to other style corpora, though example-conditioned style generation is now fairly expected.

Collaposer transforms an owned photo collection into reusable cutouts, with a story description providing additional intent. The source collection remains necessary and the interaction is understandable, but mixed source-plus-prompt asset preparation is not especially non-obvious.

A product photo conditions a generated description, which fits the pattern and transfers readily to other image-grounded writing tasks. The evidence only says that a generated result was displayed; it does not establish an artifact-ingestion interface, processing flow, or demonstrated impact.

The user supplies video and receives a generated, decomposed multitrack in one step, plainly specifying the source and generated output. The cross-modal, editable decomposition is a useful and transferable design move, although the quote does not explain subsequent repair controls.

Original physical-space footage is mandatory conditioning for video-to-video generation, supplemented by a prompt. The move plausibly enables consequential spatial reauthoring, but the evidence is truncated and does not complete the system response or UI flow.

The staged mechanism is unusually concrete: an existing SVG/raster visualization plus user intent enters a VLM, which synthesizes element-wise animation clips from that reference. It is rebuildable and transferable to other structured visual artifacts, though still jointly conditioned by text.

PicMe clearly ingests face photos and produces stylized vector portraits for downstream use. It is a clean and reusable source-conditioned transformation, but photo stylization is an obvious implementation and the evidence does not establish a strong outcome shift.

An existing text story is parsed into named fields—environment, characters, and events—and transformed through guided refinement into a structured interactive artifact. This is a particularly rebuildable, domain-transferable example of conditioning generation on a user-owned draft rather than replacing it with a prompt.

Users' prior reflections explicitly become the retrieval source for personalized assistance, a strong and widely transferable personal-corpus mechanism. The quote does not show how reflections are ingested, retrieved, or surfaced in generation, and it supplies no outcome evidence.

Users select objects from web content or a camera view and transform the selected 2D source into 3D, giving a concrete capture-select-generate interaction. Live capture still qualifies as user-facing source ingestion, although the XR and camera setup add implementation dependence.

The final images are explicitly functions of original images, prompts, and model styles, so source conditioning is present. The figure quote does not identify the ingestion interaction, clarify whether the original image is mandatory, or provide enough system detail or evidence to rate the move highly.

The current user-created 3D scene is directly ingested and transformed through lighting and post-processing changes, making it indispensable conditioning state. The mechanism is clean and reusable in scene editors, though source-aware restyling is relatively expected.

CareerCraft exposes concrete source paths—uploaded documents and reflections—and an explicit LLM transformation into predefined experience cards. The document-to-structured-record pipeline is highly rebuildable and generalizable; representativeness stops short of 5 because some free text may be authored specifically for the workflow.

Generating digital-twin responses from participant data is conceptually source conditioned and potentially transferable. However, “participant data” is unspecified, and the quote provides neither an ingestion interaction nor the encoding/retrieval mechanism needed to rebuild it; impact is also unreported.

A source image and textual description produce six novel views and per-view adherence scores, clearly specifying user inputs and system outputs. This is highly rebuildable and useful, though image-conditioned novel-view generation is a fairly standard application and not source-only.

Using the current code cell as source context for documentation is a consequential, highly transferable artifact-conditioned workflow. The supplied quote demonstrates only sending cell content to a server; the generated documentation and its dependence on that content must be inferred from the title.

RoomDreaming explicitly analyzes an existing room image with depth and segmentation estimators to recover elements and spatial state for generation. The encoding stage is concrete and consequential, but the quote omits the resulting generation and editing interaction.

A child's existing photo is transformed into a cartoon image through a predefined edit, providing an exceptionally clear source-to-output mechanism. Personal visual continuity may matter to the broader career-imagination task, but the conditioned transformation itself is an obvious one.

Text-based dream records plausibly serve as pre-existing source artifacts for generating immersive objects and environments. The quote is framed as a general technical possibility rather than a description of the paper's actual ingestion interface, so mechanism, impact, and evidential confidence remain conservative.
